matches.snippet: TDS’ Late Game Problem Introduction - Portal To Hell TDS has a late game problem; here’s why, in a massive wall of text. Already lost interest? Fine, this isn’t for you, then. If not, buckle up. DPS towers have always triumphed as the most important tower type in the game; this sentiment has grown further as more are introduced, powercreep accelerates and enemies get beefier. Feigned Variety - Desolate Dystopia As I’ve said, DPS towers define the late game. They are not only all you need, but mandatory in most cases. Bring the towers with the strongest DPS in order to overcome the late game; simple as that. The options are laid out clear for you: Gatling Gun, Ranger, Engineer, and support towers. matches.snippet: Why Ranger is better than Accelerator in most cases (Updated Post) Accelerator is currently the most overrated tower in the game. Many people think it's good because they only look at the numbers, but not their actual performance against many things. Many people say it's not overrated, but it's just them who don't know how to properly judge how good tower is. Most people would say "Oh it still has higher DPS than Ranger" which is a pretty weak argument. Today I'm bringing you all the reasons why Accelerator is Overrated and that Ranger can be better than Accelerator in most cases. Debunking Accelerator > Ranger Argument 1. It does 375 DPS. DPS doesn't mean everything. And it's not even 375 DPS, It's actually 267 DPS. The reason why is ROF Bug, it really screws every fast fire rate tower which includes Accelerator. What's more, is that Accelerator doesn't always do 25 Damage each tick, it actually does random damage ranging from 18-25. Meaning the DPS of the Lowest Damage is 270, however, with ROF Bug, it's 197. And that's a pretty significant DPS decrease there, The highest DPS Accelerator does with ROF Bug is less than the lowest DPS Accelerator does without ROF Bug. I was less worried about Minigunner since the tower and the gold variant was a bit irrelevant in the meta at that point, but I still didn't want the fundamentals of the tower to be changed and to just be a general rebalance of stats, but more of a buff. That is exactly what ended up happening and I'm very pleased with it. I was so worried because they kept calling it a rework, but it really makes me think that the developers and the community should be more careful with our wording, because I would just consider this a rebalance, as the core concept of the Minigunner being an expensive (but not extremely expensive), reliable, fast fireate, low damage, basic, above average tower for an above average price was retained. This is a good balance. It required to fill up a Scrap Meter, which it did so by just doing damage, and after it was filled up, it would build a Sentry. There could be a maximum of 2-4 Sentries per Engineer, depending on the level. As for the stats, the Engineer only cost $750 to place down, so you can actually use it for early-game defense. It also had a deadzone range where it could not attack nor build sentries, but it was very small so it just didn’t matter. The Engineer itself dealt low DPS though, and the Sentries at the time didn’t have hidden nor flying detection, but the Engineer did. It was the first tower to be upgradeable to 6 Levels.
